taste.name: Platform Identity Without Poster Contamination
taste.trigger: Showing which of a dozen-plus streaming services (each with its own saturated brand color and logo) a title belongs to, across hundreds of new titles per day
taste.decision: Chose to stamp platform identity once per group header — a single 50x50 icon plus a title count — over overlaying a platform badge on every individual poster
taste.reason: A badge on every poster would multiply a dozen competing brand colors across the same viewport at once; grouping the badge lets the poster stay pure artwork instead of becoming a logo carrier
evidence: provider icons fixed at 50x50px, border-radius 20% (366 occurrences in DOM sample), confined to icon-only elements
zero comparable badge/logo overlays detected on poster card elements
screenshot: one platform icon + '‘N titles’' precedes each horizontally-scrolling poster row, never repeated per-card

taste.name: Two-Tier Darkness Instead of Shadow Depth
taste.trigger: Separating the poster-grid surface from page chrome (nav, filters) without a lifted 'card' background that would compete with the posters' own contrast
taste.decision: Chose a two-step near-black luminance system (#060D17 page / #0A151F row surface) over drop-shadow cards
taste.reason: A shadow implies a light source and a lifted plane, which reads as app chrome; a flat luminance step reads as a dim room where the only color in the frame is the poster art and the provider logos
evidence: domData.effects.shadows returned empty for this page
backgroundColors areaPct: #060D17 at 75.8%, #0A151F at 23.4% — the entire surface is built from two flat neutrals

taste.name: Base-10 Spacing Over the Web-Standard Base-8
taste.trigger: Building a dense, filter-heavy interface (7 filter dropdowns, per-group counts, per-row carousels) that still needed to read as hand-tuned rather than mechanical
taste.decision: Standardized on a 10px spacing unit over the more conventional 8px web grid
taste.reason: 10px divides into round, human-legible steps (5, 10, 20, 25, 30) that suit chip padding and icon gaps in a data-dense filter bar better than 8/16/24/32 would
evidence: spacingDistribution dominated by 10px (729 occurrences) with 5px (27) and 25px (8) as secondary steps
no comparable frequency at the classic 8/16/24/32px marks

taste.name: Restraint: One Accent Color, Rationed to a Single Surface
taste.trigger: Owning a bright, recognizable brand yellow (#FBC500) that could have been used throughout the UI to compensate for an otherwise monochrome navy palette
taste.decision: Chose to keep yellow off every persistent UI element — nav, tabs, and filters all render in gray or teal — reserving it for the logo wordmark and one CTA (the cookie-consent 'I agree' button)
taste.reason: A page whose entire job is hosting a dozen strangers' brand colors can't also compete with its own brand color for attention; withholding yellow keeps the provider logos as the only 'colorful' elements a user has to parse
evidence: accentCandidates top value by frequency is #78A6B8 (392 occurrences), not the brand yellow
#FBC500 appears only as a single low-count background color tied to the consent button in the captured sample
